FINDING 1 — heap-buffer-overflow (1-byte OOB READ) in the lexer.

FILE: lex_unterminated_escape_oob.zen.txt — 7 bytes, NO trailing newline:
        x := "\
      (the absolute minimum is the 2 bytes `"\`.)

A string literal that is unterminated AND whose last byte is a backslash makes
the escape handler consume the byte after the backslash — which is one past the
end of the source buffer.

CMD:  ./scripts/fuzz-build.sh                       # produces ./zen-asan
      ASAN_OPTIONS=detect_leaks=0 ./zen-asan check \
        tests/fixtures/zen/fuzz-repro/lex_unterminated_escape_oob.zen.txt

OUT:  ==NNN==ERROR: AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow on address 0x... 
      READ of size 1 at 0x... thread T0
          #0 ... in at bootstrap/zenc.gen.c:45
          #1 ... in str_end
          #2 ... in scan_one
          #3 ... in scan
          #4..#20 ... in import_close (recursive)
          #21 ... in import_span_end
          #22 ... in decl_span
          #23 ... in provided_symbol_count_from
          ...
          #27 ... in module_graph
      0x... is located 0 bytes after NNN-byte region  (the source buffer,
      allocated by contents_in -> read_bytes_alloc)

CLASS: sanitizer hit / out-of-bounds read on malformed input.
       The un-instrumented ./zen does NOT crash — it reads whatever byte
       follows the malloc'd source and emits a normal parse error — so this is
       invisible without the ASan build.

          iteration 1408; reduced by hand from 558 bytes to 7.
